name: Pad Med Mamuang
steps: Rinse the jasmine rice until the water runs almost clear. Put it in a covered saucepan with 420 ml of the measured water, bring to a boil, then cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes; fluff with a fork. While it cooks, pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes. Cut onion and bell peppers into bite-size pieces, spring onion into short lengths, and mince the garlic.

Whisk soy sauce, vegetarian mushroom sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, cornstarch and the remaining 80 ml water into a smooth sauce. Check the mushroom sauce contains no oyster or animal-derived ingredients. Toast cashews in a dry pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until lightly golden, stirring so they do not burn; tip them onto a plate.

Heat 25 ml neutral oil in a wide wok or pan over medium-high heat. Lay the tofu cubes in one layer and leave them for 2–3 minutes until golden beneath, then turn and brown the other sides for another 3 minutes. Remove the tofu; cook in batches if needed so it browns rather than steams.

Add the remaining 20 ml oil. Fry the whole dried chillies for 20 seconds, then add onion and both peppers and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until crisp-tender. Add garlic and the pale spring-onion pieces for the final 30 seconds. Stir the prepared sauce again to lift settled cornstarch, pour into the pan and simmer for 1 minute until glossy.

Return the tofu to the pan and toss gently so it is coated and hot. Fold in toasted cashews and the green spring-onion pieces just before serving so the nuts stay crisp. Divide the stir-fry among four plates with the fluffy jasmine rice alongside. Leave whole chillies aside while eating if a milder dish is preferred.
tips: Pad Med Mamuang is a cashew stir-fry; this photographed vegetarian version replaces the usual chicken with distinct tofu cubes. Cashews are a major allergen. Use a vegetarian mushroom sauce rather than oyster sauce and avoid Thai chilli pastes that contain shrimp.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
